methods.description: Use the given nth-term formula and substitute every requested positive integer position in every occurrence of n, including powers/numerator/denominator; distinguish the position from the term value.

Start from the supplied initial term(s) and substitute preceding term values in order. The two-prior-term provided rule is an honest indirect extension of primary preceding-term notation, not a claimed original filled example or derived recurrence theorem.
Use the stated last term or upper position bound to recognise a finite sequence; an unbounded positive-integer position range gives an infinite sequence.

Equate the supplied term formula to the required value and solve for a positive integer position within its stated range. Check squares or matching powers for given quadratic/exponential rules; do not round a noninteger position into membership.

Apply the term condition to the provided nth-term formula, solve the inequality, and use allowed positive integer positions to count terms or select the first position; substitute that position when a value is requested.
